speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether URA has assessed the fire safety and evacuation risks arising from the temporary relaxation of the occupancy cap for private residences; and (b) what safeguards are in place to address higher turnover and foot traffic arising from the increased occupancy cap.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: For example, fire escape routes, such as common corridors and staircases, need to be well-ventilated to aid smoke dispersal during a fire.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Exit staircases are also located to provide residents with safe escape routes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Each residential unit is designed as a fire compartment to delay the spread of fire.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: First of all, how does the Building and Construction Authority monitor that the tenancy of private residence aligns with the building occupancy load requirements to ensure safety and accessibility?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Fire safety and building code risks are hard to detect in terms of safety risk breaches.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Because the overload of electrical points and all that are within the households, so, it is very difficult, even for the Management Corporations Strata Title (MCSTs) let alone the authorities to monitor and check.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The other supplementary question that I have is, what measures are in place to maintain residents' liveability?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Beyond safety, higher density also affects day-to-day liveability, because if there are multiple units within a block that have these eight occupants, common corridors, lifts and all the other facilities will be overloaded.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Even access, in terms of evacuation, within a block could be strained because a building load is of a certain capacity.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: But if there are multiple units, then we will have a problem and that is also difficult to monitor.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: On top of that, while we are looking at the common spaces, I want to reassure the Member that it also comes with a strong sense of prevention as well as public education efforts by the SCDF even in private condominium estates.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, for example, in terms of the ongoing public education efforts, to equip the community with good awareness as well as essential fire safety knowledge, it is done with the ground Community Emergency and Engagement Committees as well as the Community Emergency Response Teams.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, there are regular engagements even with the private estates.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Specific to condominiums, there are also safety and security days as well as the block evacuation drills.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: While the Member has mentioned with regard to the loading as well as the liveability as a result of the higher occupancy cap, it is the case that we are looking at it holistically – from prevention to the regulation, and subsequent to that, as part of the community engagement, increasing the emergency preparedness of all who stay within the condominiums.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
